observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2: one used automatic transaxle (front wheel drive automatic gearbox) with its torque converter fitted, shown from the bell housing side.
Photos 0 to 2: alloy casing with dust and grime, two metal cooler lines with a rubber hose printed with an SAE J1532 hose spec, a wiring connector on top, and a drive shaft output seal at the bottom.
Photos 0 and 2: a white sticker on the casing and a QR label on the torque converter, neither readable; no cast part number or ID tag can be read.
Photos 0 to 2: an orange paint mark on one torque converter bolt; no visible cracks or broken mounting ears in these angles.
Photos 0 to 2: shot in a used parts market among engines and gearboxes; watermark 'GEARUP INC', a dealer listing.
No photo of the ID tag, the oil pan, the fluid, the other side of the case or the unit running.

identity.kind: used automatic transmission (transaxle) with torque converter, fitment unconfirmed
read_from: photos 0 to 2 show the type only; no tag or part number readable

claims.evidence: No Ford logo, ID tag or part number is readable in photos 0 to 2.
No tag shown; it also sits awkwardly with 'direct from Belgium', since European and US Fusions differ.
Engine fitment cannot be read without the tag or part number.
No import papers; the seller's own words say 'American drive'.
No clip of the gearbox running or shifting in a car.
A loose gearbox carries no odometer.
No close-up of the case bolts, pan gasket or sealant to check for tool marks.

risks.risk: Gearbox may not fit the buyer's car; the model and fitment set the price.
risks.proof: Clear close-up of the transmission ID tag or cast part number on the case.
risks.if_unproven: Not priced until the tag is read.

risks.risk: Internal failure: slipping, harsh shifts, failed solenoids or valve body.
risks.proof: Clip of the gearbox fitted and driving through all gears, or a fluid sample photo showing colour and smell report.

risks.risk: Torque converter or input shaft damage.
risks.proof: Clip turning the torque converter by hand and the output shaft, showing smooth rotation without grinding.

risks.risk: Cracked casing, broken mounting ears or leaking seals on the side not shown.
risks.proof: Photos of all sides of the case and the oil pan.

risks.risk: Photos may be a dealer stock image of one unit among many.
risks.proof: Fresh photo of the unit beside a handwritten note with today's date, tag visible.
risks.if_unproven: Hold the deal until the live photo arrives.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the transmission ID tag or cast part number.
Photos of every side of the case and the oil pan.
Clip of the gearbox running in a car through all gears.
Photo of a fluid sample on white paper.
Fresh photo beside a handwritten note with today's date.
response.reason: The photos show a used automatic transaxle but no tag or part number is readable, and the model and fitment set the price, so the ID tag is needed before even a worst case price; the running and mileage claims are unproven.
